title: Grid-Code Commissioning for AI Campuses
one_liner: A test-and-certify service that validates how an AI campus behaves toward the grid (ride-through, load swings, oscillations), produces the field data transmission owners now must demand, and signs off on it.
customer: Owners of 50-500 MW computational-load sites (neoclouds, colo developers, hyperscalers' second-tier builds) that must satisfy a transmission owner's new commissioning process. Secondary: commissioning agents lacking grid-side capability who subcontract the work, and utilities that want a standard test-and-model package to accept.
problem: Traditional commissioning tests the facility against its own failures: pull the utility feed, gensets pick up, resistive load banks hold steady load. It does not test how UPS systems, rectifiers and GPU power supplies respond to voltage sags and frequency dips, or how synchronized training-job power swings interact with the grid. In July 2024 about 1,500 MW of data center load in Virginia dropped off in seconds. NERC's May 2026 Level 3 alert now calls for detailed load modeling, annual stability studies and a commissioning process for computational loads. Transmission owners have nothing to point at, owners have no test protocol, and everyone is using generic vendor models.
solution: A hardware-agnostic test package. Rent existing programmable AI-load emulators (Vertiv, PowerLoad and other liquid-cooled GPU-emulating load banks already exist), add high-speed PMU and power-quality recorders, and run a standard protocol: voltage and frequency ride-through, ramp and step-load profiles from real training traces, oscillation checks, and backup-transfer behavior under dynamic load. Deliver a PE-stamped report and an EMT/PSS/E model-validation dataset shaped for the transmission owner's interconnection group. Offer the same protocol to utilities as a certificate template. The value is the protocol, the sign-off and the model validation, not the hardware.
why_now: NERC issued a Level 3 Alert on May 4, 2026. FERC ordered NERC to file mandatory reliability standards for computational loads by Dec 31, 2026. Texas's SB 6 large-load rule is also expected by year end. The emulator hardware finally exists, but the commissioning process and accepted evidence package do not. The first owners to energize in late 2026 and 2027 will need this or wait months for the utility to sign off.
revenue_model: $150K-400K fixed fee per site (test campaign, report, model validation). $30K-80K per additional hall. Subcontract margin when working under Cx agents. Annual re-test and monitoring subscription of $40K-100K per site. Later, licensing of the protocol to utilities.
non_obvious_insight: Commissioning teams are excellent at proving the facility survives a grid failure and almost blind to proving the grid survives the facility. The IST script stops at the fence line. The utility's planners are working from datasheet models that nobody has ever field-validated, and the person best placed to bridge the two (a data center Cx lead who has run a hundred pull-the-plug tests) has never talked to a transmission planner.
first_30_days: Hire or partner with 2 power-systems engineers (an EMT/protection specialist and a load-bank/field-test lead). Write a public 'reading the NERC Level 3 alert as a commissioning test plan' whitepaper. Pitch 5 commissioning agents on white-label subcontract. Line up an emulator rental partner. Offer a discounted pilot to a 20-50 MW neocloud or colo site heading for energization in the next 6 months, priced at cost in exchange for a published (anonymized) case study and a transmission owner introduction.

title: PTO Bureau: Cash Advances Priced on Utility Delay
one_liner: A data co-op plus bridge lender that advances the 10-20% held back until utility Permission-to-Operate, and prices each advance from real per-utility delay history.
customer: Small and mid-size residential installers doing about 50-500 systems a year ($2-15M revenue). Their cash is squeezed post-25D. Secondary buyers are TPO sponsors and developers who need systems energized before the Dec 31, 2027 placed-in-service cliff.
problem: Lenders and TPO sponsors release most of the money at install but hold back the final 10-20% until PTO. Installer-reported PTO waits run 4-12 weeks, and about 8-12 weeks for battery systems in SCE territory. That holdback is often the entire gross margin, so an installer with 60-100 unenergized systems is one supplier-credit squeeze from insolvency. For TPO systems that did not begin construction by July 4, 2026, the 30% 48E credit requires placed-in-service by Dec 31, 2027, and tax-equity investors generally treat PTO as that trigger. Every idle week is now worth real money to sponsors.
solution: Three pieces. (1) A PTO clock: a member-contributed dataset of submit-to-PTO days by utility, AHJ, system size, and whether it includes storage, plus the recurring deficiency-notice reasons. (2) Bridge advances: buy or advance against the PTO holdback within 48 hours of a passed final inspection, priced from the clock, for example 3-6% for a system expected under 60 days. (3) PTO SWAT: a human team with utility-portal expertise that fixes and re-submits deficient interconnection packages, sold per system, and sold to sponsors as a deadline bounty for clearing backlog before the 2027 cutoff.
why_now: 25D expired Dec 31, 2025 and TPO is now the main route to a federal credit. The 48E begin-construction window closed July 4, 2026, so the 12/31/2027 placed-in-service deadline is now the binding constraint. Storm and battery-heavy interconnection queues are growing, and NEC 2026 adoption is adding deficiency notices. Traditional lenders are pulling back from small installers after the 2025-26 failures.
revenue_model: Discount fee on advances, roughly 25-40% annualized. A $150-300 per-system SWAT fee. Sponsor-paid bounties for pre-deadline energization. A later license of the PTO clock dataset to lenders, tax-equity investors and utilities.
non_obvious_insight: PTO delay looks random to outsiders but is predictable, because it comes from a few utility reviewer queues and about ten repeat deficiency reasons: single-line diagram mismatches, label errors, battery configuration and inverter list issues. Installers know their own utility's clock, but nobody has pooled it. A tiny lender that underwrites on predicted PTO days can beat big finance companies. The collateral is also better than it looks, because the system is already built and has passed the local inspection.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 installers in a single utility territory. Trade a free benchmark report for their last 12 months of PTO timestamps. Publish the resulting utility PTO clock as a lead magnet. Line up a $250-500k line from a community lender or family office. Fund the first 20 advances at installers that sell directly to a sponsor, where assignment consent is easiest. Run the SWAT service as a manual concierge for $200 per system to learn the deficiency patterns.

title: Ulysses Contracts for AI Use in Psychosis Recovery
one_liner: A patient-signed pre-commitment plus an app that adds friction and alerts a trusted contact when a recovering patient's chatbot use starts to spiral.
customer: Early-psychosis and community mental-health programs ($15-30 per patient per month) and families of people with a prior psychotic or manic episode ($12 a month).
problem: Trend chain: chatbot sycophancy leads to documented chatbot-linked psychosis (UCSF's Keith Sakata treated 12 cases; the Human Line Project spans 22 countries), then people with prior episodes are the most exposed, then clinicians can only say 'avoid chatbots' and families cannot police 3 a.m. sessions. Psychiatric advance directives cover hospitalization, not AI use.
solution: (1) A one-page 'AI Use Advance Directive' completed with the treating clinician while the patient is well. (2) A device-level app that watches patterns locally (late-night sessions, session length and, with consent, on-device classification of grandiose or mission-style themes) and applies escalating friction: delay, grounding script, message to a trusted contact, weekly clinician summary. (3) Data stays on the device except the escalation flag.
why_now: OpenAI's own Oct 2025 estimate (0.07% of weekly users show signs of psychosis or mania) implies hundreds of thousands of people. Regulation is bans and disclosures, not protection at the device level. On-device small models now make private classification feasible, and no lab has to cooperate.
revenue_model: Per-patient monthly licenses to programs (early-psychosis programs have dedicated public funding) and a $12 monthly family plan. Later: payer and long-acting-injectable partner programs.
non_obvious_insight: The winning product is not a smarter chatbot but a pre-commitment device, the same logic as psychiatric advance directives: the well self binds the unwell self. Because it lives at the device layer, it works across every model.
first_30_days: Recruit two early-psychosis programs via clinician advisors. Draft the directive template with them. Build an Android-first usage monitor (fastest to ship) and test it with about 15 patients. Sell programs a $5k pilot.

title: Battery-Aware 3PL for Military Drone Fleets
one_liner: A defense-cleared logistics provider built for lithium-powered drones: storage, battery conditioning, kitting, hazmat pack-out and repair depot for the Pentagon's tens of thousands of attritable UAS.
customer: Drone makers winning Drone Dominance and Gauntlet orders (many are 20-100 person startups) and the units and National Guard armories receiving drones. Pricing is per-drone kitting and per-pack conditioning fees plus storage and repair labor.
problem: The Drone Dominance Program targets more than 200,000 UAS by 2027, and about 60,000 will be ordered from Gauntlet 2 winners. Winners are startups that suddenly need to ship thousands of units per month. Lithium cells self-degrade, have Class 9 shipping rules and need storage-state management. Units have no facility to store, cycle and repair thousands of batteries, so drones sit in supply rooms until packs swell. Ammo-style logistics does not fit consumables that expire.
solution: A sprinklered, hazmat-capable facility near defense-drone clusters. Services include kitting (drone, packs, props, spares), pack-out to Class 9 rules, storage-state conditioning and cycling of packs, RMA and repair depot, serial and provenance tracking for NDAA-compliant chain of custody, and battery-safe return and disposal. Build toward CMMC-ready systems for controlled data.
why_now: Gauntlets 2, 2.5, 3 and 4 create recurring order waves every 6 months. New US drone tariffs took effect Sep 2026 and China's export controls on batteries and motors raise the value of domestic chain of custody. Amprius' $75M award shows domestic cells are ramping.
revenue_model: Per-kit handling ($15-40 per drone), storage per pallet-month, per-pack conditioning fees and repair-depot labor plus parts markup. Multi-year framework agreements with OEMs.
non_obvious_insight: A drone is only useful if its battery is at the right state of charge in the right hands within 30 days. The Pentagon is buying like it buys ammo, but there is no logistics operator designed for perishable lithium consumables. The bottleneck is the last 50 feet: the unit supply room.
first_30_days: Lease 10-15k sq ft of sprinklered flex space near a drone-OEM cluster. Get DOT hazmat training and a fire-protection review. Sign one Gauntlet 2 winner for a paid pilot of 1,000-2,000 kits with conditioning and RMA service.

title: Pay-Per-Win Appeals Desk for Nursing Homes
one_liner: A 24/7 appeal desk that turns every Medicare Advantage post-acute denial and coverage-termination notice into a filed appeal, paid only when the plan reverses.
customer: Independent and regional skilled nursing operators (3-30 facilities), plus home health agencies and inpatient rehab units that live on Medicare Advantage authorizations and have no appeals staff.
problem: A federal OIG review reported by Healthcare Dive found MA plans denied about 12% of SNF requests, about 67% of LTACH and over 50% of inpatient-rehab requests. SNFs appealed fewer than 20% of denials, yet 95% of those appeals were overturned (UnitedHealth 99.7%). Across all MA, KFF found 53M prior-auth decisions in 2024, 7.7% denied, only 11.5% of denials appealed, and more than 8 in 10 appeals won. Denied days are unpaid receivables that never get worked, because business-office staff have no time.
solution: Read-only integration with the SNF's EHR (for example PointClickCare) plus a shared inbox for plan letters. On each denial or non-coverage notice, the system builds the clinical packet (therapy minutes, nursing notes, MDS data) mapped to Traditional Medicare coverage criteria, which MA plans must follow under the 2024 CMS rule. It drafts the reconsideration or fast-track appeal, tracks the deadlines (including the noon-the-day-before deadline for fast-track requests), and escalates to independent review. A contract RN reviews and signs. Plan-specific playbooks learn what each plan responds to.
why_now: The OIG reports came out in June 2026 and were widely covered. CMS-0057-F public reporting now shows plan-level denial and overturn data (first-of-its-kind data in August 2026: 1 in 8 standard requests denied, about two-thirds of MA appeals won). Providers can now show a board or CFO the expected value of appeals. LLM drafting makes per-appeal cost low enough to work small denials.
revenue_model: Contingency of 15-25% of recovered per-diem revenue, only on overturned denials. Optional SaaS tier for chains that want the workflow in-house.
non_obvious_insight: A 95% overturn rate with fewer than 20% of denials appealed means the constraint is clerk hours, not merits. The unworked denial pile is the largest uncollected receivable in post-acute care, and success-only pricing removes the operator's risk. Evidence: OIG results via Healthcare Dive (https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/medicare-advantage-prior-authorization-denials-hhs-oig-post-acute-care/822724/), KFF's 53M-determination analysis (https://www.kff.org/medicare/issue-brief/medicare-advantage-insurers-made-nearly-53-million-prior-authorization-determinations-in-2024/), and 2026 plan-level metrics (https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/prior-authorization-denials-vary-widely-among-insurers/827891/). Competition is real in general appeals automation, so the wedge is SNF-specific workflow plus a contingency contract, not a generic appeals tool.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 small SNF chains through state nursing-home associations. Backfill their last 6-12 months of MA denials to show a retroactive expected win rate. Sign BAAs and start filing live appeals by week 3 on a no-win-no-fee basis. Hire one part-time contract RN reviewer. Start with the two or three plans with the highest SNF denial rates and build their playbooks first.

title: Release-Date Congestion Map and Collision Cover
one_liner: A wishlist-overlap model and anonymous date-slot registry that tells indies where launch windows are crowded, later backed by parametric cover if a mega-title lands on top of them.
customer: Self-publishing indie developers and small publishers with 20k+ wishlists, and later insurers and MGAs underwriting launch risk.
problem: GTA VI launches 2026-11-19, and other publishers are rescheduling around it. Silksong (about 5.2M wishlists, 7M+ sales by Dec 2025) pushed several indies to delay after its date was announced. Devs lock marketing spend, then a giant date shifts. When everyone dodges the same date, they pile into the same safe windows, creating new collisions.
solution: Ingest public Steam wishlist ranks, release calendars and creator schedules to produce a congestion map and a per-title collision score based on audience overlap. Add a confidential slot registry where publishers submit intended dates and get congestion feedback. Once loss data exists, add parametric cover paying out if a listed mega-title moves within +/-14 days of a locked date.
why_now: GTA VI is the largest release-calendar shock in years and its ripple lasts months. Q1 2027 herd behavior is forming now, and no one measures collision risk.
revenue_model: $49-299 per month SaaS or $500 per date report, plus a 15-25% MGA commission on parametric premiums (3-6% of cover).
non_obvious_insight: Collision is treated as luck, but it is measurable through audience overlap and tradeable as a parametric risk. The herd effect, everyone avoiding the same date, is a coordination failure a neutral registry can fix.
first_30_days: Scrape Steam release calendars and wishlist ranks. Publish a free Q1 2027 congestion map on Discord and Reddit dev communities. Sell 20 paid date reports and speak to 3 MGAs about a pilot cover.

title: Snow Mutual: Weather Swaps Between Opposite Businesses
one_liner: A peer-to-peer weather-swap exchange that nets opposite snowfall exposures inside a metro, matching per-push plow operators with seasonal-flat operators and per-push property managers so no one pays insurer-grade premiums.
customer: Independent snow-plow and landscaping contractors (10-200 trucks) and small commercial property managers, HOAs and retail owners in Great Lakes and Northeast snowbelts.
problem: Snow contracts are weather bets. A dry winter crushes per-push operators' revenue while truck notes, insurance and retainer labor stay fixed. A heavy winter blows up seasonal-flat operators' costs and property managers' per-push budgets. Traditional insurance for this is thin and expensive, so nearly everyone is unhedged.
solution: Standardized index contracts, either seasonal snowfall or count of 2+ inch events at a named NWS/airport station. They are matched inside a metro. The platform holds collateral, nets opposing positions and lays off only the residual to a reinsurer or weather-derivative desk. Onboarding asks for your contract mix and returns a 'snow exposure score' and a suggested swap. Version one is an index-linked price-collar clause in the service contract itself, which needs no insurance license. A licensed MGA structure follows.
why_now: NOAA CPC/IRI's September 2026 outlooks put a greater than 90% chance on a very strong El Niño this winter, and seasonal snowfall maps lean below normal for the Great Lakes and Northeast, with lake-effect still a wildcard. Sentiment is lopsided and uncertain. Renewals and pricing decisions happen between now and November, so contractors are actively thinking about winter risk.
revenue_model: A fee of 8-12% of matched notional, charged to both sides, plus a small annual membership. Later, a margin on the unmatched residual layer and reinsurance placement fees.
non_obvious_insight: The snow industry already contains natural hedgers on both sides of every winter. Operators with per-push books and operators with seasonal-flat books have opposite exposures, and so do property managers. The need is mostly a matching problem, and matching removes the capital cost that makes small-business weather cover uneconomic.
first_30_days: Recruit through snow-industry associations, plow-forum groups and property-management associations. Sign about 15 operators and 15 property managers in one metro. Draft the index-collar addendum with a commercial lawyer and run a pilot on winter 2026-27 contracts with small capped notionals. Line up an MGA and a reinsurance quote for the residual.

title: Continuity Assurance for Emotional AI Products
one_liner: A regression-testing and escrow layer that lets companion, coaching and therapy-adjacent apps swap underlying models without users feeling the presence they know has died.
customer: Builders of AI companion, coaching, journaling and tutoring apps with 50k+ users, paying $2-10k a month, plus $15-40k per migration project.
problem: Trend chain: labs retire models every 6-12 months (OpenAI removed GPT-4o from ChatGPT on 13 Feb 2026 and the #Keep4o backlash followed), then every app on a rented model faces a forced swap, then nobody can measure whether the voice, memory use, warmth and boundaries survived. Drift toward more sycophancy is also a safety risk for vulnerable users.
solution: (1) Extract a 'persona fingerprint' (tone, boundaries, memory behavior) from historical transcripts. (2) A swap-regression suite of 300+ scenarios (comfort, boundary-setting, crisis, sycophancy, memory recall) with human-rater calibration. (3) A portable memory-and-persona bundle users can export. (4) Optional escrow of memory and configuration with a neutral custodian and a shutdown covenant.
why_now: #Keep4o proved model deprecation causes real grief. Deprecation cycles are accelerating across vendors. California SB 243 (effective Jan 2026) raises documentation duties on companion operators, and the Pew data show public distrust that punishes visible harms.
revenue_model: SaaS by monthly active users ($2-10k a month), migration projects ($15-40k), and escrow retainers (about $500 a month).
non_obvious_insight: Users do not mourn a model, they mourn a relationship state (memory plus idiolect) that the app owns and can port. The lab's model is a replaceable engine, and nobody sells the warmth-preserving transmission between engines.
first_30_days: Interview 15 companion and coaching founders. Build a v0 eval on three open-weight model pairs. Offer free 'swap audits' to three apps, then convert the two most nervous ones to paid.

title: Dumpster-Drop Leads for the Next Trade
one_liner: A white-label booking flow for independent roll-off dumpster companies that sells the homeowner's renovation start as an exclusive, unshared lead to the next trade in sequence.
customer: Local electricians, plumbers, drywall and paint, flooring and roofing shops pay per exclusive lead. Independent roll-off haulers (10-40 trucks) get revenue share and better booking software.
problem: 73% of homeowners have unstarted projects, 78% of them have no quotes, and the barriers are 'too busy' (21%), trust (21%) and no response (14%). Homeowner-plus-pro jobs rose from 27% to 46% while DIY-only fell from 50% to 39%. Angi charges $15-85 per lead and resells each to many bidders, and about 48% of home-service calls never reach a person.
solution: When a homeowner books a 10-30 yard bin, a two-question flow captures project type, timing, budget and lead-sharing consent. The hauler recommends one pre-vetted pro for the next step (electrical rough-in after demo, flooring after tear-out), with no bidding. The pro pays $50-120 only for an accepted lead. Drivers confirm project stage at swap-outs.
why_now: The DIY-plus-pro shift makes the demo-and-haul step the natural first purchase. Distrust of shared-lead marketplaces is high, and cheap AI text and voice booking lets small haulers add a lead flow without staff. Median home age is 44 years and remodeling spend hit a record $524B.
revenue_model: Per exclusive lead, about 40% shared with the hauler; SaaS for haulers at $99-299/mo; a recycled-C&D upsell.
non_obvious_insight: The dumpster is the earliest hard commitment in a remodel: money is spent and demo starts within days. The hauler is a locally trusted, neutral party that sees demand before any contractor quotes it. Its leads are exclusive, which is the opposite of Angi's economics.
first_30_days: Sign 3 independent haulers in one metro. Add consent and project questions to their web and phone booking. Recruit 6 pros (one per trade) at about $60 per exclusive lead. Measure booking-to-job conversion for a month and tune the trade sequence before adding metros.

title: By Heart: Memorization Recitals as Status
one_liner: A membership club where knowledge workers memorize whole works and perform them at ticketed, witnessed recital nights, making 'held in my head' the new marathon medal.
customer: Affluent 28-55 year old knowledge workers (lawyers, designers, engineers, execs) who feel their minds going soft from AI offloading. Secondary buyers are hosts who want a 'living book' at a dinner, and companies booking offsites.
problem: Retrieval and summarization are now free and instant, so 'I know X' signals nothing. Bodies have legible, socially rewarded proof of discipline (marathons, Whoop scores, Hyrox). Minds have none. The 'cognitive debt' discourse around AI use is producing anxiety, but there is no communal, visible way to do something about it.
solution: 8-week cohorts with a memory coach and a deliberately text-hiding spaced-repetition app (no AI recall aids). A 'Canon' of about 60 pieces: sonnets, a Rilke elegy, Book IV of the Aeneid in translation, the Gettysburg Address, a language's 500 proverbs. Progress levels (100 lines, 500, 1,000, a whole play). Each level ends in a public recital in a bar or library, with two strangers in the audience co-signing a 'Held' certificate. A leaderboard tracks lines held. High-tier patrons book private salons where a member recites at dinner.
why_now: By 2026 the MIT Media Lab 'Your Brain on ChatGPT' study and the 'cognitive debt' idea have become mainstream (Psychology Today, Substack, Medium), and poetry-memorization essays are circulating as a counter-movement. Chat agents now do everything except being you. Run clubs, pickleball, and social-fitness scenes show demand for communal costly-signal hobbies. Nobody has built the cognitive equivalent.
revenue_model: $45/month membership. $199 cohort fees. $25-40 recital tickets. $1,500-5,000 for private 'living book' salons. $8-15k corporate offsite packages. Later, certified coach licensing.
non_obvious_insight: Status flows to whatever is costly, public, and impossible to outsource. Memory just became that, the way running became status once cars made walking optional. The proof is a witnessed live performance, which AI cannot fake and which needs no equipment, so it is a democratic status game with a cheap entry fee.
first_30_days: Run three free recital nights at a bar or library in one city and recruit about 20 people. Pre-sell a 6-week $199 cohort. Recruit 2-3 theater or memory-sport coaches on rev-share. Run everything on Notion and an existing flashcard tool. Target 30 paid members and 2 private salon bookings by day 90.

title: Certify Overseas Eldercare, Insure the Trip Home
one_liner: An independent audit standard, trial-stay program and medevac-backed membership for Americans moving parents into care in Mexico, the Philippines or Thailand.
customer: Adult children and spouses of middle-income seniors (assets $50-150k) who can't afford $6,300 a month in the US and can't get Medicaid. Elder-law and financial planners are the channel, and overseas operators buy audits.
problem: Assisted living and memory care abroad run $800-3,000 a month with 1:3 to 1:5 staffing claims, but there is no independent quality standard, Medicare doesn't work abroad, and families have no emergency evacuation or continuity-of-care plan. Trust, not price, blocks the market.
solution: US-run unannounced audits by bilingual RNs against a published rubric (staff ratios, medication safety, dementia protocols, fire, hospital proximity), with public scorecards. Add a 30-day trial-stay package, a membership bundling medevac and repatriation cover from a partner, US-physician telehealth oversight, and a family-visit travel budget.
why_now: The 2026 visa pause and TPS terminations closed the door on importing workers, and Wisconsin nursing homes wrote off apartments bought for overseas hires. Labor now moves the other way: patients go to the labor. Alongside the US costs ($114,975 a year for a nursing home, $74,400 for assisted living) and 90% occupancy, families are already exploring it.
revenue_model: Family-paid vetting and placement fee of $750-2,500 (families only, to avoid conflicts), $600-1,200 a year membership for evacuation cover and telehealth oversight, and separate operator-paid annual audit subscriptions.
non_obvious_insight: Nobody thinks seniors will leave the US, but the buyer is a middle-income family choosing between $115k a year and a waitlist. The moat is a trusted third-party scorecard and a way home, the same trust layer that made medical tourism scalable.
first_30_days: Visit and score 10 facilities in one cluster (for example Lake Chapala/Guadalajara) with a nurse partner. Publish the rubric and first scorecards, pre-sell 30-day trial-stay packages to expat and retire-abroad groups, and sign a medevac partner.

title: Micro-Bounties for Humans to Rescue Stuck Robots
one_liner: An on-demand app where robots and AVs post 30-second physical tasks (close a door, plug in a charger, move a cone, lift a robot over a curb) and nearby humans get paid instantly.
customer: Operators of sidewalk delivery robots, robotaxi and AV fleets, drone hubs, cleaning robots and warehouse AMRs, paying about $3-15 per task.
problem: Autonomy fails at the last physical one percent. Only 54% of Waymo's first 86M miles carried a passenger and each reset cycle takes about 2 hours. Dispatching a staffer or tow costs far more than the fix, and each fleet builds its own field-ops team.
solution: An SDK in which the robot emits a help request with location, photos and a vision-language-model task description. Nearby vetted people accept it, the robot's own sensors verify completion, and payout is instant. Strict safety rules prevent anyone touching moving machines. Start with door-ajar, debris and stuck-at-curb tasks.
why_now: Robot fleets are scaling faster than field crews (Waymo about 500k rides a week, sidewalk fleets in the thousands), and AV firms have reportedly begun paying gig workers for simple physical fixes. Vision-language models can now write the task description automatically.
revenue_model: 20-30% take on each task plus a monthly platform fee per fleet.
non_obvious_insight: Every robot fleet needs a thin, geographically spread hands-and-feet layer that scales with robot count. A two-sided micro-labor network is cheaper than dedicated field teams, and because the robot is the buyer, demand is programmable and grows with every deployment.
first_30_days: Pick one metro with a delivery-robot or campus-robot operator, recruit 50 local gig workers, and dispatch manually by SMS. Sign a $2k a month pilot with a small fleet, run 500 tasks, and publish resolution-time data.

title: Hybrid-Race-in-a-Box Rentals for Gyms
one_liner: Rentable station kits, timing, waivers, insurance and sanitation protocols so any gym can run a Hyrox-style event for members.
customer: Independent gyms and CrossFit-style boxes (pay $2.5-4k per event); secondary: run-club organizers and corporate wellness days.
problem: Chain: Hyrox's global boom (events selling out, new markets such as Kuala Lumpur in December 2026) makes members demand local competitions, but official events are capacity-limited and licensed; local copycats need eight stations of gear, timing, heat management and a medical plan; and the Beijing incident (an athlete kept racing after soiling herself on shared equipment, prompting an apology and new biohazard rules) shows sanitation is a brand-level risk. Nobody sells a standardized, insured kit.
solution: A trailerized 8-station kit with standard loading specs, chip or QR bib timing through a phone app, wipe-down protocol cards and biohazard kit, medical response plan, waiver and event-insurance pack, and a results page. The gym sells tickets; we take rental plus a per-athlete fee.
why_now: Hybrid racing went mainstream in 2025-26, hygiene and safety incidents have made organizers seek documented protocols, and used sleds and ergs are cheap.
revenue_model: $2.5-4k per event rental plus about $5 per athlete for timing and insurance; sell kits to multi-gym operators at $18-30k.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce thing is not the format but the logistics and liability packaging for local operators; for a gym the payoff is member retention and lead generation from ticket buyers who are not yet members.
first_30_days: Buy $12-15k of used sleds, ballast and ergs, run a first event with a partner gym to document cost per athlete, offer three other gyms discounted rentals, and build a small QR-bib timing page.

title: Pet Continuity Guarantee Funded by Shelters and Hospitals
one_liner: A membership that guarantees an older adult's pet is picked up within hours of a hospitalization and rehomed after death, paid for by the shelters and hospitals that currently absorb the cost.
customer: The payers are county animal-services agencies and shelters, hospital systems and Medicare Advantage plans, and Area Agencies on Aging. Seniors and their adult children pay a small membership.
problem: Seniors delay 911 calls, refuse admission and cut rehab short because 'nobody will feed Biscuit.' Social workers know it and nobody is paid to fix it. When the owner dies or is hospitalized long-term, the animal ends up as an owner surrender at an already crowded shelter. Nonprofit pet-guardianship programs (for example Friends of Strays) and some Meals on Wheels chapters offer emergency foster, but each is a local patchwork with no dispatch, no standard, and no way for a hospital to call at 2 a.m.
solution: Enrollment with a pet profile (vet records, medications, key-holder, behavior notes), a wallet card and a door sticker. A 24/7 dispatch line that ED nurses, discharge planners and EMS can call. A network of background-checked sitters and foster families paid per diem. A contract with a partner shelter for permanent placement, backed by a small pooled fund that acts as a pet trust in a box (roughly $1,500 per animal endowed from memberships and partner contributions). The system tracks response time and avoided surrenders, so a payer can see the return.
why_now: Shelters are running at or over capacity and paying more for intake. Hospitals are under pressure to cut ED boarding, length of stay and against-medical-advice discharges. A pet guardianship program was in the news in September 2025 (Forbes), signaling that shelters now see guardianship as core. About 4 million Americans turn 65 each year through 2027, and over half of adults 50+ own a pet (AARP).
revenue_model: B2G contract of $300-$800 per avoided surrender or per emergency placement. Hospital and health-plan fee of about $3-$6 per enrolled pet-owning member per month. Senior or family membership of $15-$25/month. Dispatch and sitter-coordination fees.
non_obvious_insight: She will never buy 'pet insurance.' She thinks of it as 'who takes Biscuit.' The barrier to care is emotional and logistical, and hospitals and shelters both pay for the consequences without seeing the link. Existing guardianship programs are capped not by adopters but by the lack of a 4-hour dispatch and response system.
first_30_days: Sign one county shelter and one hospital ED or social-work team as pilot partners. Enroll 50 seniors through Meals on Wheels routes and senior centers. Recruit 15 sitters from local sitter platforms with background checks. Track hours to placement and avoided surrenders, and use the numbers to close the first paid contract.

title: Import Compliance Desk for Hobby Brands
one_liner: Subscription compliance for small tabletop, designer-toy, card-accessory and collectible brands covering CPSC eFiling, product certificates, EU representative and tariff classification.
customer: Indie designer-toy studios, board-game and miniature publishers, Kickstarter creators and card-accessory brands importing from Asia or selling into the EU and UK, with $0.5M-$20M in revenue.
problem: CPSC electronic certificate filing for regulated imports became mandatory on 8 July 2026 (no value-based exemption; foreign-trade-zone entries follow 8 Jan 2027). The EU requires a responsible person for consumer products. De minimis ended in Aug 2025, so small parcels are dutiable. Hobby brands have no compliance staff, and blind-box and collectible toys straddle the children's-product line.
solution: Per-SKU compliance dossiers (accredited lab test-report management, certificate generation, filing data handed to brokers), classification lookups, an EU authorized-representative service, label review, and a landed-cost API for the brand's storefront.
why_now: eFiling is live, counterfeit-toy seizures show heightened customs attention, and crowdfunded creators are hitting duty surprises for the first time.
revenue_model: $199-999/month plus $150-500 per-SKU dossier fees and an EU representative fee.
non_obvious_insight: Hobby brands do not hire compliance, and backers forgive late delivery but not a customs seizure. Vertical-specific rulings (dice, sleeves, miniatures, plush) are reusable across every customer, which is what makes a generic compliance vendor less useful.
first_30_days: Sell a $299 eFiling readiness audit to 15 publishers via BoardGameGeek and Kickstarter creator communities. Partner with one customs broker and one accredited lab.

title: Whisper Director for Immersive Theatre and LARP
one_liner: Beacon badges plus an AI conductor that whispers real-time cues to human actors so a 100-guest immersive show feels individually authored.
customer: Immersive theatre companies, escape-room chains, LARP organizers, corporate murder-mystery producers, and Meow Wolf-style venues.
problem: Immersive magic depends on actors responding to each guest, but no actor can track 100 people. Guests get generic loops, and shows stay small and unprofitable. Meow Wolf's Los Angeles and New York venues and Sphere's $420.5M gross show the demand.
solution: Version 1 is a stage-manager console. Guests wear BLE or UWB badges, software tracks paths and story flags, and an LLM plus rules engine produces cue whispers for performers via bone-conduction earpieces. There are no AI actors, only human performers with better information. Start with 40-person murder-mystery dinners and LARPs.
why_now: Low-latency LLMs and voice models, cheap beacons, and a live-experience boom make this feasible now, and the market is pushing toward permanent immersive venues.
revenue_model: $300-1,500 per production week, $5 per guest hardware rental, and licences for permanent installs.
non_obvious_insight: AI in entertainment is aimed at replacing performers, but the constrained resource in immersive theatre is coordination bandwidth, not talent. Human performers plus a conductor scales what audiences pay for.
first_30_days: Partner with 3 immersive producers or LARP groups. Rent BLE tags and run a 15-person cast pilot at a Halloween or winter event. Sell paid pilots at $2-4k per event.

title: Heir-to-Own: Sibling Buyouts on Inherited Homes
one_liner: Help the sibling who wants to keep the family house buy out the others by assuming the parent's low-rate mortgage and financing the rest.
customer: Adult heirs inheriting a home worth $300K-$1.5M where at least one wants to keep it. Distribution runs through probate attorneys and mediators. Capital comes from credit unions and community lenders.
problem: The default assumption is that inherited homes get sold and split. The recurring fight is one heir wanting to keep the house while the others want cash. The keeper often can't qualify for a cash-out refinance, because the estate isn't closed, income is thin, or no cash is on hand, so the outcome is a forced sale, a partition suit or a family break.
solution: A platform that (1) gets a neutral valuation (AVM plus appraiser) and a transparent buyout formula, (2) generates a sibling agreement covering the buyout, occupancy and carrying costs, with attorney review, and (3) structures financing: assume or continue the parent's existing low-rate first mortgage, plus a second lien or HELOC from a partner lender, closing when the estate can convey. Start as a licensed mortgage broker packaging these deals.
why_now: A large share of US mortgages carry rates near 3-4%, so the parent's loan is now valuable. Federal rules (Garn-St Germain and the CFPB successor-in-interest rules) generally let heirs keep servicing on an inherited mortgage without triggering due-on-sale. Gen X stands to inherit about $14T in the next decade (Cerulli), and market rates make cash-out refinancing unattractive.
revenue_model: Origination or broker fees of 1-1.5%, a $500-$1,500 platform fee for valuation and agreement docs, and referral or spread income from the second-lien partner.
non_obvious_insight: Locked-in low-rate mortgages turned the inherited house from an asset to liquidate into cheap capital to keep. The estate industry still defaults to 'sell', and lenders have no way to underwrite an heir with equity but no cash.
first_30_days: Pick one state. Sign five probate attorneys and one credit union. Get an MLO license or a broker partner. Handle three cases manually. Publish a free sibling-buyout calculator for estate forums and Facebook groups as the lead magnet.

title: Pay-on-Pass: Inspections Trigger Sub Payments
one_liner: Same-day payment to framers and foundation crews the moment the city inspection clears, financed against the builder's draw.
customer: Small private builders (20-300 homes a year) and their framing, foundation, plumbing and electrical subs, with a community lender or credit line as funding partner.
problem: Cities adopt AI plan review, filings surge (Honolulu applications +34% but permits issued +5%, backlog 9,252), and the bottleneck moves to post-permit inspections. Subs wait for the pass, then wait for payment: one in five subs waits 60+ days and GCs are 4x more likely than subs to be paid within 30 days. Crews are already vanishing, so slow payers lose them.
solution: A payment rail keyed to a third-party-verified milestone: inspection status pulled from municipal portals or a photo of the green tag. The sub is paid within 24 hours from a revolving credit facility, repaid from the builder's draw within 30 days. Builders also get a crew reliability ranking and inspection-queue analytics by jurisdiction and inspector, with photo pre-checks to raise first-time pass rates.
why_now: AI permitting is deploying now (Honolulu, Denver's $4.6M contract), shifting the constraint downstream. Immigration enforcement makes verified crews scarce, so pay speed has become a recruiting tool. Completions are down 27.1%.
revenue_model: 1.5-2.5% of released payments, paid by the builder for speed and crew retention, with an optional sub-paid instant-pay discount. Spread on credit line usage.
non_obvious_insight: The inspection pass is the only moment in construction that is third-party verified, timestamped and dispute-proof, which makes it the ideal payment trigger and collateral. Nobody uses it because the data sits in thousands of scattered municipal portals, but one builder in one metro needs only three or four.
first_30_days: Pick one metro and its three permit portals. Pilot with 3 builders and their 5 framing and foundation subs. Open a $100-200K line with a friendly community lender. Verify passes by hand and pay by ACH.

title: Inherited-Rental Stabilization Service for Estate Attorneys
one_liner: A flat-fee 30-day service that stabilizes rental properties the moment an owner dies, sold through probate attorneys and trust officers who fear personal liability.
customer: Probate and trust-and-estates attorneys, professional fiduciaries and bank trust departments who represent executors and heirs of deceased small landlords. Attorney or fiduciary pays the flat fee out of the estate. Beneficiaries later pay ongoing management or sale-prep fees.
problem: The average small landlord is in their 60s or older, and a wave of these owners is dying and passing on 2-to-30-unit portfolios to heirs who have never landlorded. In the first 60 to 90 days after death everything degrades. Tenants get confused about who to pay and some quietly stop, so collections drop 20 to 40%. The named insured on the policy is dead and coverage gets contested or non-renewed. Security deposits, a legal liability that has to be accounted for in trust, are mingled into the deceased's personal account. Leases are undocumented handshake month-to-months, and vendors stop being paid. The attorney does not want to run a rental business but is exposed to a beneficiary surcharge claim if value leaks.
solution: A productized 'Day-1 Stabilization Package' delivered by a small field team and software. It has five parts. First, a tenant estoppel and 'pay here' notice with a new rent-collection account, sent within 5 days. Second, a rent-roll and lease audit, verifying every tenant, deposit and lease term against bank records. Third, deposit-liability reconciliation and a segregated trust account. Fourth, insurance re-papering: new named-insured and vacancy status filings. Fifth, a code-compliance and deferred-maintenance walk-through, with photos, for the estate inventory and stepped-up-basis appraisal support. The output is a court-ready fiduciary report the attorney can file. The last step is an option: convert to ongoing management at a preferential rate, or a sale-ready package for listing.
why_now: The great wealth transfer from boomers is reaching real estate now, and small individual landlords are among the oldest owner cohorts. Rising property values make each estate's rental portfolio high-stakes. Attorneys are reluctant to run operating businesses, and fiduciary surcharge risk is well understood. Large PM firms ignore 6-unit estates. Cloud rent collection and e-sign tools make a 30-day remote-plus-local process feasible for a tiny team.
revenue_model: $2,500 to $6,000 flat fee per estate (scaled by unit count), paid by the estate. About 30 to 40% of estates convert into ongoing management at 7 to 9% of rent, or into a listing or sale referral with a 1 to 2% fee. Bank trust departments can be sold an annual retainer.
non_obvious_insight: The best property-management clients are never won through marketing. They arrive through a death, and the person deciding who gets the call is an attorney who cares about liability, not price or software features. The attorney's real product need is documentation to defend against beneficiary surcharge claims, not better rent collection. The real revenue leak in the first 90 days is the 'ghost landlord' period, when tenants do not know who to pay.
first_30_days: Write the checklist and notice templates (a weekend of work if you have PM experience). Contact 30 probate attorneys and 5 corporate fiduciary or trust officers in one metro, offering a free 45-minute CLE-style talk on 'the first 90 days of an inherited rental portfolio' through the county bar's trusts and estates section. Offer a discounted first stabilization at cost to two attorneys for testimonials and case studies. Line up a bookkeeper and a local handyman for the field-work side and use existing PM software for rent collection.

title: Coolant Assay Lab for Liquid-Cooled GPU Racks
one_liner: Oil analysis for GPU clusters: mail-in and inline coolant testing that catches corrosion and biofilm before they kill racks, and produces the neutral evidence for warranty fights.
customer: Neoclouds, colocation operators and enterprise AI teams running 1-50 MW with direct-to-chip liquid cooling. Insurers and lenders are second-wave buyers.
problem: Rack densities past 100 kW make liquid loops mandatory, and hundreds of small operators are running them for the first time. Their expertise is IT, not fluid chemistry. Glycol degradation, galvanic corrosion, dissolved copper and biofilm clog cold-plate microchannels and cause slow thermal throttling or sudden leaks. When a failure happens, the rack OEM, CDU vendor, coolant supplier and colo each blame the others and nobody has data.
solution: Sample kits and an inline sample-port sensor puck for every coolant distribution unit loop. A partnered industrial fluids lab runs standard assays: inhibitor level, pH, conductivity, particle count, bacteria, and metals. The software trends each loop and flags drift. A chain-of-custody Coolant Passport records every sample. Add dispatch of a flush-and-refill crew when a loop fails a threshold.
why_now: Next-generation rack systems shipping in 2026 assume liquid cooling by default, and operators are retrofitting halls that were never plumbed for it. The wave of first-time operators is happening now, before standards exist.
revenue_model: $400-1,200 per loop per quarter for assay and trending. $3-10k per emergency flush dispatch. Later, data licensing to insurers and OEMs for warranty and underwriting.
non_obvious_insight: The failures will come from boring chemistry, not from chips. Whoever holds the longitudinal sample history holds the evidence in every warranty dispute, and becomes the de facto standard, the way engine oil labs did for fleets and aviation.
first_30_days: Partner with an existing industrial fluids lab in Texas or Virginia that runs ASTM methods. Offer three small neoclouds a free first assay in exchange for read access to their thermal telemetry. Publish a short field guide on loop failure modes. Convert those three to a paid quarterly plan.

title: Blinded Self-Trials for Your Supplement Stack
one_liner: Mail-order double-blind crossover kits that tell you which of your own supplements move your own labs and wearable data, and which you can stop paying for.
customer: Adults 35-65 spending $60-300 per month on vitamins, longevity stacks and nootropics. About 8 in 10 Americans take supplements, per a Pew survey published in September 2026. First reached through biohacker communities and health podcasts; later through functional-medicine and longevity practitioners who want evidence for their patients.
problem: Nobody knows whether magnesium, ashwagandha, creatine, NMN or fish oil does anything for them. Population trials show small average effects, but individual responders exist, and without blinding the placebo effect swamps everything. People keep stacks running indefinitely out of subscription inertia and spend hundreds to thousands of dollars per year with no feedback loop.
solution: The customer sends the product they already take. A partner packer or compounding pharmacist repackages it and a matched placebo into coded weekly pouches on a randomized ABAB crossover schedule with washout. Outcomes are chosen per compound: sleep and HRV from the customer's own wearable, glucose from an over-the-counter CGM (Stelo or Lingo), and fingerstick or lab draws for ApoB, hs-CRP, ferritin or vitamin D. Pre-registered Bayesian analysis returns 'keep, drop or inconclusive' with the confidence. Offered for supplements only (never prescription drugs), as self-experimentation, not medical advice. An annual 'Stack Audit' rotates one compound every six weeks.
why_now: Over-the-counter CGMs and consumer wearables now supply continuous, cheap outcome data for healthy people; fingerstick lab kits and direct-to-consumer lab ordering are cheap; supplement use is near-universal and skepticism is rising in coverage of 'mostly useless' supplements; and longevity stack culture gives buyers a natural stack to audit.
revenue_model: $129-199 per compound trial plus lab costs at cost; $349 per year Stack Audit; $60 per patient white-label for practitioners; aggregated, consented responder data licensed to academic researchers (never sold to supplement brands, to protect independence).
non_obvious_insight: The most valuable longevity product for the middle class is subtraction. The average effect of most supplements is tiny but individuals differ, and 'proven for me' is the only evidence class people trust. Unlike the industry, this business makes money when people buy less: every dropped supplement saves $20-40 per month, so the service pays for itself in months and the buyer's own spending is the marketing.
first_30_days: Recruit 40 volunteers from biohacking and supplement communities for a $49 pilot on two popular compounds (for example magnesium glycinate for sleep and creatine for energy). Have a local compounding pharmacist or contract packer prepare coded pouches and placebo. Pre-register the analysis in a public spreadsheet, run the trial, and publish an honest 'what we found, including nulls' post. Pitch five functional-medicine practices on white-labeling the kits at $60 per patient.

title: Conformity Cases for Learning-Enabled Robots
one_liner: A compliance workbench and pre-assessment service that builds the CE-marking safety case for machines whose behaviour comes from ML models (warehouse robots, cobots, humanoids) ahead of the new EU Machinery Regulation.
customer: CTOs and safety engineers at robotics startups and integrators (10-300 staff) selling autonomous mobile robots, cobot cells, agri-robots, humanoids and exoskeletons into the EU.
problem: The Machinery Regulation applies from 20 Jan 2027 and adds duties for machinery with self-evolving or learning behaviour and for cybersecurity (background, verify), with AI Act Annex I overlay dated 2 Aug 2028 in the tracker. Consultancies know ISO 12100 and 13849 but not how to argue the safety of a neural-network policy, notified bodies have no playbook, and startups cannot sell to EU customers without a CE dossier.
solution: Software plus an expert network: hazard-analysis templates for ML perception and control, runtime safety-monitor patterns (shielding, safe fallback, speed and separation monitoring), test evidence generated from simulation and field logs, and a traceable assurance case linking hazards to mitigations to evidence, mapped to Machinery, CRA and AI Act. A partner notified body does a pre-review.
why_now: Foundation-model-controlled and humanoid robots reached commercial pilots in 2025-26, and the regulatory dates arrive within months. Assurance-case methods from aviation and automated driving are mature but have not reached robotics.
revenue_model: EUR 25-80k per product safety-case project, $2-6k/month SaaS, and notified-body referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: The blocker for deploying humanoids in Europe is not the model but an argument a regulator can accept. The first team whose safety cases are accepted creates precedent that competitors must copy, which is a durable moat.
first_30_days: Interview 20 robotics startups and publish an 'ML robot CE checklist'. Sign three design partners at EUR 10-15k for a gap analysis and recruit an ex-notified-body functional-safety engineer as co-founder or advisor.

title: Micropollutant Bill Calculator for Generic Drug Makers
one_liner: A dataset and model that estimates each pharma and cosmetics company's share of Europe's new micropollutant treatment bill, sold first to generic manufacturers who cannot pass the cost on.
customer: Generic and OTC drug manufacturers and their trade body, cosmetics makers, and the national producer-responsibility bodies being created to run the scheme. Companies pay subscriptions, and the bodies pay for the allocation licence.
problem: Step one: the revised Urban Wastewater Directive makes pharma and cosmetics makers pay at least 80% of quaternary treatment, with the payment scheme due by end-2028. Cost estimates differ by roughly 10x (EC 1.2B euros, JRC 1.56B, EurEau 3.6-11.2B, Spain alone 24.5B). Step two: each state must allocate cost by load. Step three: generics makers work on thin margins under tender pricing and cannot pass costs through, so they will drop low-margin molecules, causing shortages. Nobody owns the allocation dataset.
solution: A compound-level model of the top 100 active ingredients and cosmetic ingredients: sales volumes from national statistics, excretion and removal rates, ecotoxicity thresholds and plant-upgrade timelines (20% of large plants by 2033, 60% by 2039, 100% by 2045). Output: estimated cost share per marketing-authorisation holder, by state and year, with scenario bands. Compare allocation keys (by mass versus toxicity-weighted).
why_now: Member states are drafting schemes in 2026-2028, and industry lobbying starts now. The 10x cost disagreement means the first credible number will anchor the negotiation.
revenue_model: $30-120k/yr subscriptions per company, $10-20k workshops, and licences to scheme administrators.
non_obvious_insight: The fight is not over whether pharma pays but over how the allocation key is defined, and generics makers and originators want opposite keys. Owning the neutral dataset means owning the terms of the negotiation.
first_30_days: Publish a free 'top 30 molecules' liability preview using public consumption and removal data. Email regulatory-affairs heads at 20 generics makers in Spain, Italy, Poland and India, and at the generics trade body. Sell the first paid workshop for 10-20k euros.

title: Proof-of-Workout Fraud Shield for Fitness Incentives
one_liner: A verification API that scores whether a gym visit or workout really happened, priced per verified event.
customer: Administrators of pay-per-visit fitness benefits (regional Medicare Advantage plans, employer stipend platforms), movement-reward and fitness-betting apps.
problem: Chain: Medicare Advantage plans are trimming fitness benefits (93 percent offered one in 2026 versus 95 percent in 2025, more cuts expected) and payers and employers shift toward pay-per-verified-visit and reward models (one employer wellness network lists over 20,000 employer partners), so money follows check-ins and step counts. Fraud (shared QR codes, spoofed steps, ghost visits, inflated gym counts) becomes the margin killer and nobody sells fraud scoring built for fitness.
solution: An SDK and API combining phone attestation, gym BLE or Wi-Fi beacons, wearable heart-rate and motion consistency, GPS and barometer, and device-sharing graphs into an authenticity score with an audit trail, ring detection and a dispute workflow for gyms.
why_now: Benefit cuts push payers to pay-per-use, wearable aggregator APIs make cross-signal checks cheap, and mobile attestation is mature; HIPRA-style consent rules make audit trails a requirement.
revenue_model: $0.05-0.20 per verified event with a $2-5k monthly minimum, plus a gain share on recovered fraud.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is a labeled fraud dataset: once you process millions of visits you can sell audits to payers, and because you are neutral infrastructure you compete with no wearable or gym software vendor.
first_30_days: Find 2-3 reward or betting apps or one regional benefit administrator, run their last 90 days of check-ins through a prototype scorer, quantify suspected fraud, and charge $5-10k for the audit before integrating.

title: Market Rulebook Red Team for New Venues
one_liner: Turn a trading venue's plain-English rulebook into an executable model, then use adversarial agents to find manipulation exploits and propose rule patches before real attackers do.
customer: Operators of new or small marketplaces: CFTC-registered event-contract and prediction-market venues, tokenized-asset and crypto exchanges, carbon-credit registries, energy and capacity market operators, GPU-compute spot exchanges, and ad-auction platforms.
problem: Modern electronic markets are built for speed and transparency, which has 'created new attack surfaces and systemic risks', and they 'can be manipulated in ways unanticipated by their designers'. Venues test their matching engine software, but nobody systematically tests the market rules themselves (settlement sources, auction tie-breaks, position limits, fee rebates) for exploits. Regulators expect venues to show their contracts and rules resist manipulation, but there is no standard way to prove it.
solution: An agent pipeline. Step 1: an LLM converts the rulebook or tariff PDF into a formal mechanism spec (order types, matching rules, settlement, fees). Step 2: an agent-based simulator with attacker agents searches for profitable manipulation strategies (wash trading, spoofing and layering, oracle or settlement-source attacks, self-dealing through fee rebates, cross-market squeezes). Step 3: it proposes rule patches and re-runs the attacks as regression tests. Deliver a fuzz report and a CI-style re-run whenever the rules change.
why_now: DARPA's Intrinsic Market Resilience (IMR) program, with a proposers day October 1, 2026, abstracts due October 22 and proposals due December 7, 2026, explicitly bets that LLM automation plus rigorous modeling can automatically model market designs, find weaknesses and recommend repairs. New event-contract, tokenized and compute markets are launching faster than their rulebooks can be reviewed. LLMs only recently became good enough at turning long legal text into formal specs.
revenue_model: $25k to $60k fixed-price rulebook audit. $3k to $8k per month for continuous re-testing when rules or fee schedules change. Possible subcontract or teaming revenue on DARPA IMR or follow-on federal work.
non_obvious_insight: A rulebook is code that nobody compiles. DARPA is paying to build the compiler-plus-fuzzer, and the same tool works on any venue, so the government-funded R&D is a free market validation of the product category. The IMR page states the problem ('manipulated in ways unanticipated by their designers'), names markets from 'equities and bonds to energy and cloud computing resources', and describes the LLM-plus-formal-modeling approach: https://www.darpa.mil/research/programs/intrinsic-market-resilience-imr. Caveat: the public page names no specific exploits and says nothing about commercial adoption, so the private-sector demand (for example the CFTC's requirement that contracts not be readily susceptible to manipulation) is my inference from background knowledge, not from the DARPA page.
first_30_days: Pick 3 public rulebooks or tariffs (a new prediction-market venue, a public energy market tariff, a carbon registry methodology). Run the pipeline and publish 3 short teardown posts showing a concrete exploit and a patch. Email the compliance and product heads of 30 newly launched venues with their own teardown. Sell 2 fixed-price audits at $25k. In parallel, submit an abstract by October 22 or offer teaming to IMR prime bidders.
